excerpt: Kudos is a US money app that picks the best credit card for each purchase and, on Premium, has AI negotiate bills and cancel forgotten subscriptions. What's new in 3.0, pricing, refunds and alternatives.
content:
Kudos is a money app for people in the US with several credit cards. Its free version picks the card that earns the most rewards for each purchase at more than 2 million merchants, adds extra cashback (Kudos Boost) at over 15,000 partner stores, surfaces card perks you may have forgotten, tracks balances and due dates and shows a free credit score. It works as an iPhone and Android app and a browser extension.

Kudos Premium adds the features this launch is built around: an AI agent that phones your providers to negotiate lower bills, automatic cancellation of subscriptions you no longer want (Kudos asks before cancelling anything), automatic activation of card-linked offers at American Express, Chase, Citi, Capital One and Bank of America, and an AI assistant, in beta, that answers questions about your spending and cards. Kudos 3.0, launched on Product Hunt on 12 October 2026, reorganised the app around a single "Your wins" total and a ranked "next best move". It finished #8 for the day with 119 upvotes.

Kudos is made by Kudos Technologies, Inc. of California, co-founded by Tikue Anazodo and Ahmad Ismail. It makes money partly from affiliate commissions, including on purchases through Boost and on credit-card applications, so its recommendations can involve paid relationships. It covers US cards and bills, so it is of little use to readers in India or elsewhere.

We have not tested Kudos ourselves. This page brings together Kudos's help centre, terms and App Store listing (its main website loads only in a browser), its Product Hunt page and the official pages of comparable apps, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: iOS/iPadOS 16.4 or later; Android; Chrome extension. US cards and providers
profile.starts_at: Free; Premium sold in the app (App Store lists $24.99/month or from $53.99/year)
profile.summary_short: US money app that picks the best credit card per purchase and, on Premium, negotiates bills and cancels subscriptions
use_cases: Using the right credit card at checkout to maximise rewards
Getting card-linked offers activated without doing it by hand at each bank
Having an AI agent call a provider to ask for a lower bill
Finding and cancelling subscriptions you forgot about
Seeing all card balances, due dates and credit score in one place

paragraphs: Tikue Anazodo says he spent years in consumer payments at Microsoft, Google and Affirm, and kept noticing that people don't lose money because they're careless but because claiming it is a chore: the credit they forgot, the bill that crept up $40, the subscription they meant to cancel. In his words, most AI assistants launched this year help you spend, and Kudos is built to get money back.

Members told the team the app made them do too much of the work, so Kudos 3.0 was rebuilt around one question: what is the most valuable thing you can do with your money right now? He said Kudos never moves money without your OK, and that you keep all the savings from negotiations. The savings figures he quoted from early testing are the company's own and we have not verified them.

fit: live in the US and carry several rewards credit cards
want card offers activated and bills negotiated without doing it yourself
are comfortable linking card and transaction data to an app
not_fit: live outside the US: the supported card issuers and bill providers are American
don't want to share purchase and card data (the App Store privacy label lists data linked to you, some used for tracking)
want to try Premium before paying: its terms say there's currently no free trial, though first-time yearly subscribers have a 90-day savings guarantee

pricing.intro: The core Kudos app is free. Kudos does not publish Premium prices on its website; its terms say pricing may change. The prices below are the in-app purchases shown on its US App Store listing on 14 October 2026.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: Card selection, Boost cashback, card perks, dashboard, credit score, checkout autofill

plans.name: Premium (monthly)
plans.detail: App Store in-app purchase; the terms describe monthly billing as a legacy option

plans.name: Premium (yearly)
plans.detail: The App Store lists several yearly price points; AI bill negotiation, subscription cancellation, offer auto-activation, Kudos AI (beta), 1.25x Boost

notes: No per-negotiation fee on Premium or Lifetime; the terms say you keep 100% of any savings.

Premium fees are generally non-refundable. First-time yearly subscribers can claim a full refund between day 90 and day 120 if Kudos hasn't saved them more than the subscription cost (90-Day Savings Guarantee). Contact Kudos before cancelling.
Boost points are not money until redeemed, redeem from 1,000 points, and expire unless you earn at least 10 points in each 365-day period. Non-Premium PayPal redemptions carry a $2.99 fee.

alternatives.intro: Rocket Money is on Product Hunt's alternatives list; MaxRewards and CardPointers are closer card-optimiser apps. Prices come from each product's own pages, checked on 14 October 2026. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: MaxRewards
items.what: Tracks rewards, benefits and card-linked offers and tells you which card to use
items.starts_at: Platinum from $20/month or $240/year (pay what you want), 7-day trial
items.difference: Card optimisation without a shopping-cashback programme or AI bill negotiation.

items.name: CardPointers
items.what: Picks the right card for bonus categories and auto-adds offers from six major US issuers
items.difference: Adds card offers without asking for your bank logins.

items.name: Rocket Money
items.what: Budgeting, subscription tracking and cancellation, and bill negotiation
items.starts_at: Free plan; Premium on a choose-what-you-pay scale
items.difference: Charges a fee of 35 to 60% of first-year savings for bill negotiation, and doesn't pick cards for you.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Monarch, Honey, My Financé and Coupert.

faq.a: The core app is free: card selection, Boost cashback, perks, a dashboard and a credit score. Premium adds AI bill negotiation, subscription cancellation, offer activation and the AI assistant.
Kudos doesn't publish the price on its website. On 14 October 2026 its US App Store listing showed $24.99 a month, yearly prices from $53.99 to $91.99, and lifetime access at $190 or $199.

faq.q: Does Kudos cancel subscriptions without asking?
faq.a: No. The co-founder said on Product Hunt that you are always prompted before any subscription is cancelled.

faq.q: How does the AI bill negotiation work?
faq.a: On Premium, Kudos's AI calls your provider to ask for a lower rate within your current plan. You must be the authorised account holder, calls may be recorded where legal, and results aren't guaranteed. There's no per-negotiation fee.

Premium fees are generally non-refundable. First-time yearly subscribers can claim a full refund between day 90 and day 120 if Kudos hasn't saved them more than the subscription cost. Lifetime purchases are non-refundable.
Not in a useful way. It is built for US credit cards, US issuers' offers and US bill providers.
From Premium and Lifetime purchases and from affiliate commissions, including on Boost purchases and credit-card applications. Its terms say merchants may also pay to be featured.
